topic: Graph-budget sharp counterfactual envelopes under bounded failures of context-independent inverse transport. Fix a finite-horizon shared-order scalar triangular SCM on a finite parent-context grid, mutually independent uniform ranks, rational continuous strictly increasing piecewise-affine conditional quantiles, rational-box factual evidence, and bounded rational piecewise-polynomial payoff. Put an orientation gate on every reachable mechanism-context cell; connect grid-neighbor cells in H and impose TV_H(s)≤K. Characterize attained sharp endpoint hulls for the conditional intervention payoff, zero-budget point recovery, nesting, exact Boolean-polynomial/polyhedral-integration computation with complexity or hardness bounds, and simultaneous DKW-projection inference. Report the smallest K changing each DoFlow or CausalSim decision without claiming K is identified. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Common factual ranks reduce each counterfactual reflection to products of factual and rollout orientation gates. Integrating the rational piecewise model gives an orientation-independent Boolean polynomial of degree at most twice the number of nonintervened mechanisms; an augmented factor graph then supports budgeted tree-decomposition optimization. Exact checks recovered the two-context sign-flip envelope and four-cell path endpoint pairs (-1/5,-1/5), (-1/5,2/5), (-3/10,2/5), and (-3/10,1/2) for K=0,1,2,3. Destructive checks covered disconnected graphs, non-strict nesting, changing downstream contexts, cycles, vacuous unconditional queries, ineffective encodings, zero cells, and small evidence probabilities; no matching literature collision surfaced. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a terminating certified DKW outer-projection algorithm that preserves shared quantile reuse, changing context cells, payoff discontinuities, and the conditioning denominator, and contracts pointwise to the sharp endpoints. EARLY KILL TEST: Compare enumeration, polynomial compilation, and shrinking DKW enclosures on the four-cell witness and a two-stage rational example with a context switch and threshold payoff; excluded exact values or persistent noncontraction require pivot or stop. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_signedtransport_switchbudget_bounds.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a terminating certified DKW outer-projection algorithm for graph-budget sharp conditional counterfactual endpoints that preserves shared quantile reuse and changing rollout contexts, handles discontinuous payoffs and the conditioning denominator, and contracts pointwise to the exact endpoint hull.

open_problems.why_unsolved: DKW controls each empirical CDF uniformly, while the prior shared-coupling run shows that coverage must be obtained by inverting one simultaneous law region before endpoint optimization. Neither line supplies a finite shrinking fiber for reused inverse quantiles: one rank can enter factual and rollout mechanisms, rollout can switch parent-context cells, threshold payoffs are discontinuous, and conditioning makes the objective fractional. The first proof step must therefore replace projection of a fixed multinomial polytope by certified cell refinement of simultaneous CDF bands; coordinatewise DKW coverage alone does not show that every compatible shared-quantile SCM remains enclosed or that projected endpoints contract when the positive factual-event denominator is estimated.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite refinement-and-optimization algorithm returning rational outer endpoints with simultaneous finite-sample coverage, a termination certificate at every tolerance, and pointwise convergence of both outer endpoints to the attained sharp endpoints whenever the factual-event probability is positive and all reachable cell sample sizes diverge.

writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The causal payoff is set identified -> sampling perturbs the compatibility restrictions -> optimizer faces and active contexts can switch -> project one simultaneous shrinking law region to obtain honest endpoint inference

open_problems.why_unsolved: Autobounds polynomializes finite discrete SCMs, and pseudo-Boolean theory supplies generic width-based tractability and hardness, but neither establishes the causal compilation produced by exact integration of continuous piecewise-affine shared-rank mechanisms. The prior compiler attempt identifies the concrete failure: duplicating a latent selector across summands permits different SCMs in different branches, while maximizing before probability integration changes the endpoint. The first proof step must build one orientation variable per reachable mechanism-context cell, encode H-disagreements and the global K budget without copying selectors, and prove a legal sum-before-max elimination invariant. Intervention-induced context switches can add higher-order payoff factors, so ordinary treewidth of H need not be the controlling parameter.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A polynomial-size rational factor circuit, an objective-preservation theorem and legal sum-before-max elimination invariant, an explicit constrained-width runtime and bit-complexity bound with backpointers yielding an attaining SCM, and an NP-hardness or parameterized-hardness theorem when the controlling width is unbounded.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest identification paper treats context-independent inverse transport as an all-or-nothing restriction, while counterfactual-sensitivity work relaxes latent distributions rather than the structural transport map. The unentered assumption class allows a bounded number of graph-local orientation disagreements while reusing the same rank across factual and rollout worlds. Conditioning adds a common positive denominator, and intervention-induced context changes make the relevant orientation products query dependent. The located literature does not prove attainment, zero-budget collapse for this class, or criteria separating weak nesting from strict endpoint expansion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp partial-identification theorem expressing both conditional-payoff endpoints as attained extrema over TV_H-bounded orientation fields, with an exact K=0 recovery clause and necessary-and-sufficient criteria for equality or strict expansion of successive endpoint hulls.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Complete-identification theorems require transport agreement across all mechanism contexts, whereas TV_H(s)=0 forces equality only within connected components of H. A specified conditional query can touch a strict subset of cells, with factual abduction and counterfactual rollout traversing different components. The banked face-aware criterion says a target is identified when constant on the exact compatibility fiber, but its multi-district converse failed because locally legal faces need not glue globally. The first proof step must replace linear row constancy by constancy of a fractional Boolean-polynomial payoff on the exact zero-budget shared-rank fiber; if constancy fails, both orientation assignments must decode to legal observationally equivalent SCMs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if criterion stated through a query-induced context-incidence graph and constancy of the payoff on the exact TV_H=0 fiber, with a constructive pair of observationally equivalent legal SCMs having unequal rational payoff values whenever the criterion fails.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Breakdown-frontier methods study smooth relaxations such as c-dependence, divergence, or a defier share, while the prior decision proposal changed an information set rather than the admissible mechanism class. Here the first proof step is an integer value-function analysis over nested graph-cut budgets: one added disagreement can change several cross-world products, endpoint equality may persist for multiple K values, and disconnected H creates plateaus. Local derivatives and interpolation cannot identify the first strict decision crossing. The dominant problem is structural-SCM sensitivity, with partial-ID breakdown analysis secondary; K is an analyst-chosen assumption budget, not a parameter identified from the observed law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite exact algorithm and correctness theorem returning, for every declared decision rule, the least K producing a strict endpoint-boundary or robust-action change (with tie and infinity conventions), together with attaining orientation assignments, rational crossing witnesses, and simultaneous confidence statements for the decision-stability conclusions only.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The rejected modulus angle shows that semialgebraic stratification and a nonzero endpoint discriminant provide, at most, sufficient regularity and not a characterization of projected calmness or the sharp exponent on singular cells. The destination adds a finite union over orientation faces, reused inverse quantiles, context-switch boundaries, payoff jump surfaces, and a factual-event denominator. Its first proof step must replace a polynomial response-fiber coderivative by a target-restricted error bound for this union of fractional piecewise-polynomial images. Positivity controls the denominator but does not rule out optimizer-face switches or tangential contact producing slower Hölder rates.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient target-restricted regularity criterion with computable local Lipschitz or Hölder exponents and matched perturbation sequences proving sharpness, yielding the exact pointwise rate at which DKW outer-endpoint excess vanishes.

literature_map:
1. Tan, Chen, and Du (2026, arXiv:2605.04413) is the closest anchor: context-independent inverse transport plus local invertibility gives complete counterfactual identification, while local invertibility alone fails.
2. Chen and Du (2025, ICML; arXiv:2505.02212) formalize exogenous isomorphism as a sufficient route to complete layer-3 identification in bijective and triangular monotone SCMs.
3. Maiti, Plecko, and Bareinboim (2025, AAAI) show that counterfactual identification under monotonicity can be query- and graph-specific.
4. Christensen and Connault (2023, Econometrica) derive sharp global counterfactual sensitivity extrema over neighborhoods of latent-variable laws, not transport-map failures.
5. Duarte et al. (2024, JASA; arXiv:2109.13471) reduce discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs with certified enclosing and epsilon-sharp ranges.
6. Zaffalon et al. (2024, IJAR) map a tractable subclass of discrete-SCM counterfactual bounds to credal networks and emphasize general inference hardness.
7. Del Pia and Khajavirad (2024, arXiv:2410.23045) locate pseudo-Boolean tractability and hardness through signed-hypergraph structure rather than causal semantics.
8. Liu and Ihler (2013, arXiv:1302.6584) show why marginalization and maximization require constrained elimination orders.
9. Massart (1990, Annals of Probability) supplies the sharp distribution-free DKW primitive for simultaneous empirical-CDF bands.
10. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica; arXiv:1601.00934) give calibrated inference for projections of partially identified parameters.
11. Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis (2024, NeurIPS) separate representation, sampling, and optimization errors in continuous causal partial identification.
12. Masten and Poirier (2020, Quantitative Economics; arXiv:1705.04765) define breakdown frontiers as analyst-indexed robustness objects and provide inference.
13. Noack (2021, arXiv:2106.06421) constructs monotonicity-violation-indexed sharp LATE bounds and robust regions.
14. The located literature does not combine shared factual ranks, graph-TV orientation failures, conditional-payoff ratios, exact Boolean integration, and finite-sample DKW projection in one model class.
